prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 华东区门店2024年1—5月销量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "门店" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 92px
  col 2: header "1月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "2月" · longest unbreakable word 34px · one-line width 34px
  col 4: header "3月" · longest unbreakable word 34px · one-line width 34px
  col 5: header "4月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 6: header "5月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare monthly sales across East China stores and reveal each store's month-to-month trend over January–May.","reading":"Readers scan row by row to identify a store, then read left to right across the five months; they also compare a single month vertically across stores. The row-label column anchors each row, while the month columns form one continuous comparable series.","groups":["Column 1 (门店): row-label column identifying each store.","Columns 2–6 (1月–5月): one comparable time series; keep near-equal widths and consistent alignment so month-to-month differences read cleanly."],"keep_intact":["Month headers 1月–5月, unbroken.","All numeric sales values, with no wrapping, truncation, or overflow.","门店 header and the full characters of every store name; store names may wrap but must not be truncated."],"may_wrap":["Store names such as 上海徐汇店 and 南京新街口店 may wrap at Chinese character boundaries; row height can absorb two lines.","Month headers and numbers should not wrap."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [81, 56, 55, 55, 56, 56] · table 360×394px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [74, 57, 57, 57, 57, 57] · table 360×394px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [68, 58, 58, 58, 58, 58] · table 359×394px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"The row-label column is the widest of the three (81px), and all five month columns are identical in width, so the time series still reads as one comparable unit. The result is an unbalanced budget: width was taken from the columns that must stay legible (the numbers) and handed to the column that cannot use it.","cause":"Month widths of 55px leave only 34px of text space for content that needs 35px — below the safe minimum. Month columns at 57px give 36px of text space — 1px of slack over the 35px requirement — so every 4-digit value and every 1月–5月 header sits clear of the borders while all five months stay exactly equal. Col 1 at 74px gives 53px of text space, comfortably fitting three characters (45px) with ~8px of breathing room, so names break 3+2 or 3+3 without a lone orphan character on the second line. Rows read as coherent units.","problems":"No structural fault.
